sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 10.0% a year, from $129 billion in FY2017 to $303 billion in FY2026 [F203][F1][F10].
Operating income grew faster at 12.3% a year [F204], lifting operating margin from 3.2% in FY2017 to 3.9% in FY2026 [F23][F32].
FY2021 revenue grew 17.5% [D189], as net sales rose 18% on a 16% comparable sales increase, with strong non-foods and e-commerce [P56][P54].
FY2022 revenue grew 15.8% [D238], attributed to a 14% comparable sales increase, new warehouses and higher inflation than in earlier years [P42].
Warehouse ancillary and other businesses contributed +3.7pp of FY2026 growth [D601], against +0.5pp in FY2025 [D598], as sales rose 19.9% [D600].
The 10-K says these businesses grew faster than core merchandise categories, but it gives no separate cause for the FY2026 jump beyond sales mix [P12].
Food and Sundries remains the largest category at 38.5% of FY2026 revenue and added +2.6pp to growth [D558][D560].
FY2026 net sales rose 10%, driven by comparable sales up 8% (average ticket up 5%, frequency up 3%) and 25 net new warehouses [P14][D434].
Operating income grew 12.5% against revenue growth of 10.1% [D435][D434], an incremental operating margin of 4.7% [D457].
Diluted EPS grew 14.0% [D438], just above net income growth of 13.9% [D436], because the diluted share count changed by only -0.1% [D452].
Operating margin of 3.9% in FY2026 equals the window high, against a 3.4% median and 3.1% low [F32][D691][D692][D690].
That margin ranks in the 17th percentile of six retail peers, whose median is 5.0% [D32][D709][D710].
In FY2026 cost of revenue moved operating margin by -0.0pp and SG&A by +0.1pp [D459][D460]; SG&A fell 10 basis points as a share of sales [P9].
Gross margin percentage fell three basis points in FY2026 as faster growth in gasoline and pharmacy shifted sales mix [P12][D459].
The window's largest margin rise was +0.3pp in FY2024 [D349]; cost of revenue added 0.4pp [D361] as charter shipping charges did not recur [P24].
FY2026 operating cash flow of $15.8 billion was 1.71x net income, and free cash flow of $9.38 billion was 1.02x [F82][D421][F102][D422].
Free cash flow conversion of 1.02x compares with a window median of 0.99x, and the 3.1% free cash flow margin with a 2.8% median [D422][D701][D418][D698].
Operating cash flow rose from $13,335 million to $15,817 million on higher operating income and faster inventory turns with better supplier terms [P6][F81][F82].
Capex reached 2.1% of revenue and 2.41x depreciation, up from 1.83x in FY2017 [D417][D423][D11].
Net cash rose to $15.1 billion in FY2026 from $9.50 billion in FY2025 [D427][D378].
Net cash is 5.0% of revenue, the 100th percentile of six retail peers, whose median is -4.4% [D428][D715][D716].
Current debt rose to $2,248 million from $75 million [X160][X159], while cash and equivalents of $20.2 billion cover it [F142].
Buybacks plus dividends were $3,306 million, or 35.2% of free cash flow, with buybacks at $848 million [D429][D430][X110].
The diluted share count was 444.4 million against 440.9 million in FY2017, so repurchases only offset issuance [X100][X91].
No red-flag candidates were supplied and the data checks reported none, so no data-quality flag applies.
Receivables grew 23.6% in FY2026 against revenue growth of 10.1%, after 17.7% and 19.1% in the two prior years [D455][D434][D406][D357].
The cited filings do not explain the receivables growth; receivables are still only 5 days of sales [D431], so the issue is persistence, not size.
Capex growth of 17.0% in FY2026 outpaced revenue, and capex to depreciation rose to 2.41x from 2.11x in FY2024 [D441][D434][D423][D325].
Two years of capex running ahead of depreciation raises the depreciation cost base that must be absorbed to hold the current margin [D423].
Operating margin holding at or above 3.9% [D691] in the FY2027 10-K would confirm leverage; a fall to the 3.4% median [D692] would reverse it.
Receivables growth below revenue growth, against 23.6% versus 10.1% in FY2026 [D455][D434], would ease the concern in the FY2027 10-K.
Free cash flow to net income falling below the 0.99x window median [D701], from 1.02x [D422], would show capex outrunning earnings in the FY2027 10-K.
